newsitem.title: CHINA: China migrant population seen at 100 million.
newsitem.headline: China migrant population seen at 100 million.

text.p: China's floating population of migrant workers may have grown to 100 million people, far more than the official total, the China News Service on Monday quoted the Ministry of Civil Affairs as saying.
Under-reporting and other factors had led to the miscounting of the huge army of rural Chinese who have flooded cities and towns in search of work, the agency said.
While official statistics have long put the number of migrants at around 80 million, population experts believed another 20 million could be going unrecorded, it said.
The agency gave no details of how the estimate was made. Ministry of Civil Affairs officials contacted by telephone declined to comment.

Migrants have poured into most of China's cities to work as labourers and to do other jobs looked down on by newly affluent urban residents, but officials say the influx has also weakened social order and boosted crime.

While a large degree of migration was the inevitable result of economic reform, where the human tide was not carefuly channeled it was causing social problems and weakening China's strict population controls, the China News Service said.
"In areas that have not formed effective management of the floating population, such hideous phenomena as illegal unmarried cohabitation, bigamy and prostitution are breeding and spreading," it said.
As well as provoking family disputes and raising divorce rates, unregulated migration was weakening the state family planning policy that limits urban residents to one child per couple, it said.
Many unregistered migrant families, are able to evade the fines and censure that are supposed to follow any breach of the rules on child numbers.
More than 90 percent of the migrant population were young people at or near marriageable age, the agency said.

"If effective steps are not taken, illegitimate births and early marriage and child-bearing among the floating population ...will severely hit the the basic state family planning policy and the continued healthy development of the economy," it said.
China already has the world's largest population with 1.2 billion people, and the number is growing more rapidly than state-set targets despite the tough one couple, one child family planning policy.
